domain_symbols.fluid_field: velocity, pressure, density, and forcing fields

rules.name: Continuity equation seed
preconditions: The continuum-fluid model and density and velocity fields are fixed
rules.operation: Express local mass conservation by the continuity equation.
examples: Local density change is balanced by mass flux divergence
counterexamples: Replacing div(rho u) by an unrelated scalar source term without changing the model is invalid

rules.name: Incompressibility criterion rule
preconditions: The standard incompressible constant-density regime is active
rules.operation: Enforce incompressibility by zero divergence of velocity.
examples: Divergence-free velocity fields preserve local volume in the incompressible model
counterexamples: Declaring every constant-speed flow incompressible is invalid

rules.name: Navier-Stokes structural seed
rules.output_form: -grad p + nu Delta u + f with div u = 0
preconditions: The standard viscous incompressible regime is active
rules.operation: Represent viscous incompressible flow by the Navier-Stokes momentum balance and incompressibility constraint.
examples: Viscosity enters through Laplacian smoothing while pressure enforces incompressibility constraints
counterexamples: Removing the pressure term without changing the constrained flow model is invalid

rules.name: Reynolds transport theorem seed
preconditions: A moving control volume and transported extensive quantity are fixed
rules.operation: Differentiate moving-domain integrals through Reynolds transport structure.
examples: Transport identities bridge particle and control-volume descriptions of fluid motion
counterexamples: Differentiating a moving-domain integral as though the domain were fixed is invalid

rules.name: Vorticity curl rule
preconditions: The standard three-dimensional differential-operator setting is active
rules.operation: Define vorticity as the curl of velocity.
examples: Rigid rotation has nonzero vorticity even when speed is spatially simple
counterexamples: Treating vorticity as div u is invalid

rules.name: Bernoulli along streamlines seed
preconditions: The standard steady inviscid incompressible hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Apply Bernoulli conservation along streamlines in the classical ideal-flow regime.
examples: Pressure, kinetic, and potential terms trade off along a streamline in ideal flow models
counterexamples: Applying Bernoulli unchanged to arbitrary viscous unsteady flow is invalid

rules.name: Euler equation seed
preconditions: The inviscid continuum-fluid regime is active
rules.operation: Model inviscid flow through Euler momentum balance.
examples: Ideal-fluid dynamics arise as the zero-viscosity structural limit of the viscous balance law
counterexamples: Dropping viscosity while keeping viscous boundary effects unchanged is invalid

rules.name: Reynolds number seed
rules.input_form: flow scale, speed, density, and viscosity data
preconditions: Characteristic scales and viscosity are fixed
rules.operation: Compare fluid regimes by the Reynolds number.
examples: The same governing equations can exhibit very different regimes depending on whether viscous or inertial effects dominate
counterexamples: Comparing flow similarity without matching the governing nondimensional balance is invalid

rules.name: Kelvin circulation seed
rules.input_form: transported loop in an inviscid barotropic conservative-force flow
preconditions: The standard Kelvin theorem hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Conserve circulation along transported loops under the standard inviscid hypotheses.
examples: Vortex transport can be constrained by circulation structure instead of only by local velocity inspection
counterexamples: Arbitrary viscous forced flow does not automatically satisfy Kelvin circulation conservation

rules.name: Boundary layer seed
rules.input_form: viscous wall-bounded flow with high Reynolds number
preconditions: A wall-bounded high-Reynolds-number regime is fixed
rules.operation: Localize strong viscous effects to thin boundary layers near walls.
examples: Near-wall flow may remain viscosity-dominated even when the bulk flow is largely inertial
counterexamples: Treating the full domain as uniformly boundary-layer scaled is invalid

rules.name: Acoustic perturbation seed
rules.input_form: small compressible perturbation of a fluid background state
preconditions: A compressible background state and small-perturbation regime are fixed
rules.operation: Derive acoustic wave behavior from linearized fluid conservation laws.
examples: Sound propagation can be derived from fluid conservation laws rather than introduced as a separate unrelated field law
counterexamples: Arbitrary finite-amplitude turbulent flow is not automatically governed by linear acoustic perturbation equations

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
